claims.summary: For a connected graph side S in a maximum-degree-Delta>=2 graph, k>=2Delta boundary edges and arbitrary F3 charges, any private spanning-tree flow with all chords zero uniquely solves the side on its boundary-charge promise. Common substitution preserves Boolean/parity operations and reuse, but some substituted private edge indicator realizes MOD3-zero on floor(k/(2Delta)) Boolean bits by constant-size boundary substitutions lying entirely in that promise. Weighted tree-centroid proof. Every connected bounded-degree n>=4 graph has a proof-independent connected bipartition with both sides >=n/(2Delta); uniform expansion then gives k=Omega(n). Generic literalwise fixed-depth flow substitution is therefore impossible at polynomial size. Separate existential projections also fail MP when an internal cycle supplies different private witnesses.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter graph/weighted-tree and exact Boolean restriction proof, medium reviewed. Credits the old connected-side projection and circuit theorem. This tests a generic semantic normalization, not extraction from arbitrary Frege, not all proof-dependent witness choices, and not old PC quotient evaluation.
claims.rationale: Resolves the scheduled nonlinear projection test: one common flow repairs logic but has a hard literal even on compatible inputs, so an extraction must use proof information beyond this normalization.
claims.next_action: Test correlated private-witness annotations with explicit MP/copy/parity and projection costs against the existing trace/ladder controls; do not infer a small circuit from small witness size.
